prompts.text: Seedance 2.0 on @yapper_so Prompt; Ultra-realistic cinematic night sequence, shallow depth of field, neon bokeh reflecting on wet pavement, atmospheric subway-street setting. A stylish young woman in her early 20s walks along a lively night street near a subway entrance. She has shoulder-length dark hair slightly moving in the breeze, expressive eyes, subtle makeup, confident yet relaxed presence. Medium close-up framing. She holds a bright orange smartphone in one hand while casually carrying a white coffee cup in the other. Streetlights, restaurant signs, and passing traffic cast soft orange-teal reflections across her face. The city ambience feels alive — distant chatter, neon signage, taxis passing, steam rising from subway vents. Camera remains steady in a smooth forward tracking shot. No cuts, no zoom. Cinematic lighting, shallow focus isolating the subject from the vibrant night background. Without warning, a deep metallic vibration echoes beneath the street. The pavement begins to tremble. A massive circular underground hatch violently blasts upward from the asphalt, spinning into the air as sparks and dust scatter across the street. Pedestrians panic and scatter in confusion while the woman pauses, calmly looking upward with curiosity rather than fear. The metal hatch slams back down with tremendous force. The street fractures open, concrete splitting apart. From the underground tunnel emerges a gigantic alien creature — roughly elephant-sized, with biomechanical skin patterns, glowing internal veins, and a threatening stance as it climbs out of the shattered roadway. Extreme close-up of the creature’s face: textured alien skin, mechanical muscle fibers moving beneath the surface, heavy breathing and glowing eyes. Cut to an extreme close-up of the woman’s face — composed, focused, completely fearless. She slowly pockets her phone and tosses the coffee cup aside. Instantly, a futuristic combat suit begins assembling across her body — sleek white armor forming piece by piece with micro-mechanical precision. Glowing icy-blue energy lines run through the suit as crystalline frost particles swirl around her. The helmet forms with a reflective visor and luminous accents. The alien charges forward, smashing parked cars and pushing taxis aside, causing destruction across the street. At the last possible moment, she vanishes in a flash of freezing energy — a teleport burst of shimmering ice particles. She reappears behind the creature mid-motion. The creature turns — and she delivers a devastating punch. Extreme hyper slow-motion impact shot: shockwaves ripple across the alien’s face, skin deforming under the force, fragments and particles bursting outward with dramatic motion blur. Hero Moment: The woman floats mid-air in a powerful superhero stance, surrounded by swirling frozen debris and luminous ice shards. The alien creature shatters into fragments around her, illuminated by neon reflections and cold blue energy. The camera slowly orbits around her, maintaining cinematic framing as ice particles drift through the air and reflect the city lights. She gently descends back to the street with controlled precision. As her feet touch the ground, the white combat armor dissolves into glowing particles that fade away, restoring her normal appearance seamlessly. She straightens her jacket slightly, regains her relaxed posture, and resumes walking down the neon-lit street as if nothing happened. Around her, stunned pedestrians stand frozen in disbelief, silently watching her disappear into the glowing night city. Cinematic ending, soft ambient city sound, the mysterious hero walking calmly into the distance.

prompts.text: Seedance 2.0 Prompt on @yapper_so SUBJECT A lean, martial-arts–trained chef with sharp facial structure and closely cropped hair. His wardrobe blends a contemporary Chinese chef uniform with kung-fu training gear: a sleeveless fitted top with a mandarin collar in dark matte fabric that catches light subtly, forearms wrapped with cloth bands for grip and control, loose tapered trousers allowing deep stances, and soft kitchen shoes suited for silent movement. His body proportions emphasize long limbs and flexible wrists; elbows deliver explosive strikes. Every action follows a deliberate combat rhythm—brief stillness, sudden acceleration, then a locked finish—supported by grounded stances and fast pivoting footwork. ENVIRONMENT A traditional Chinese open-flame cooking station. An iron wok rests permanently on the burner. A polished metal counter reflects the warm lighting. A blue-and-white porcelain bowl sits centered in the foreground. Lighting combines warm overhead illumination with strong flickering firelight from the stove. Thin oil smoke drifts through the air while heat shimmer subtly distorts the background. MOOD Focused intensity. Movements feel disciplined, aggressive, and precise—closer to a martial performance than casual cooking. Nothing chaotic; every motion feels intentional and controlled. TIMELINE 0:00–0:02 Extreme close-up from a wide POV. The chef stands behind the counter, which remains between him and the camera. He steps forward, compresses his posture, then sharply lifts his head and locks eyes with the lens. Both hands grip a mass of dough. With one clean pull he stretches it outward, folds it once, then pulls again. The dough begins separating into a small set of evenly forming strands. 0:02–0:05 Cut with slight handheld energy. The chef keeps the noodle bundle under full control between both hands. Through smooth fold → align → stretch movements he extends the strands into clean parallel lines. Roughly 8–12 thin noodles arc outward and sweep close past the lens. He completes the final stretch and lays the aligned noodle bundle neatly onto the counter. 0:05–0:07 Camera shifts with a brief recoil before stabilizing. The chef glides sideways behind the counter. One palm sweeps across the surface, sending shrimp and greens into the air and directly into the waiting wok. The wok never leaves the stove; he grips only the handle. Any stray ingredient is intercepted and redirected smoothly into the pan. 0:07–0:10 Single continuous shot. The chef manipulates the wok entirely through wrist control and momentum. No hands enter the pan. He lifts, tilts, and snaps the wok so the ingredients rise, spin, and land back inside. His elbow strikes the stove edge—sparks scatter briefly. He presses the wok down into the flame, then pulls upward, drawing the fire into a second controlled flare. 0:10–0:12 Match-movement tracking shot. Still gripping the wok handle, he pivots his stance. With his free hand he retrieves the noodle bundle from the counter and drops it into the wok in one clean motion. He immediately resumes tossing: three crisp cycles—fast → faster → sudden stop. Shrimp, greens, and noodles visibly combine while sauce coats everything evenly. 0:12–0:15 Cut to a steady POV. Total stillness. The chef tilts the wok and slides the finished dish into the porcelain bowl—revealing glossy noodles, plump shrimp, and vibrant greens. He lifts the bowl toward the camera until it fills the frame. One finger taps the rim, creating a faint vibration. Steam rises quickly and expands until it completely fogs the lens, ending in a soft fade.

prompts.text: A high-energy fifteen-second continuous single-take visual effects short. A lone surfer rides atop a massive translucent light-whale, diving through a vast floating ocean suspended in the sky. Music is ethereal electronic pulses, each beat synchronized with visual shifts. Physical continuity is absolutely clear. The light-whale's body flows like liquid glass, with shifting bioluminescent currents pulsing within. Camera starts at an ultra-low angle rushing toward the surfer's feet, the crystalline board slicing through suspended water, droplets arcing outward in curved trajectories. The surfer's toes grip the board, every muscle twitch visible. Camera climbs rapidly up the whale's glowing spine. Its skin is transparent like, internal light pulsing like breath. Camera cuts hard to an extreme close-up of the surfer's face—only eyes and brow, background dissolved into light streaks. Wind pressure flutters her eyelashes, pupils slightly contracted from speed. Her gaze is intense and alive. They plunge downward through layers of floating water-islands and suspended tides. Camera whips right, capturing them skimming between two colossal floating coral structures, their surfaces pulsing with slow light. Slow motion activates: jellyfish the size of buildings drift past the lens, tentacles stretching into silk-thin trails of light. The surfer shifts weight on the crystalline board, carving along the whale's twisting back. The whale begins a spiraling dive through vertical suspended currents. Camera orbits them at high speed, rotation synchronized with the spiral, the floating ocean background stretching into cyan and gold light bands. The whale's eye now forms—not a traditional eyeball, but every bioluminescent vein in its body suddenly converging toward its head, forming an incandescent core of light. The core contracts then expands, like a pupil focusing. Camera cuts hard to an extreme close-up of this light-core. It is gazing at the surfer, as if checking she is safe. They burst through a dense field of glowing plankton. Particles explode outward, trailing behind like stardust. The whale breaches a suspended waterfall, the water body shattering into billions of floating droplets. Super slow motion: every droplet hangs frozen mid-air, refracting golden sunlight, the surfer's hair leaving a reflection on each droplet's surface. The surfer flips her body, threading through a gap barely wide enough for one person between two converging tidal streams. Camera cuts to a side profile—only inches between her and the crushing water. Time resumes at full speed. Floating reefs pulse like heartbeats, airborne fish schools shift like galaxies, distant sky currents ripple like breathing oceans. Golden sunlight pierces through layers of suspended water, refracting into moving beams that dance across every surface. The whale arcs upward, breaching through the sky-ceiling into open air. In the final moment, the whale looks back—the light-core at its head pulses once, like a farewell—then releases a radiant ring of light that ripples outward across the entire floating ocean. Camera pulls back rapidly, the silhouettes of whale and surfer consumed by light. Frame freezes at the farthest edge of the expanding light wave. Rules: New composition every single second. Must include: surfer eye extreme close-up, feet-on-crystal-board close-up, whale light-pupil extreme close-up, suspended water droplet close-up. Music is ethereal electronic pulses synchronized to visuals. No humans clipping. No text or watermark. Let AI freely interpret light refraction and droplet trajectories.

Subtle realistic chest rises and falls synchronized with breathing. Shallow depth of field with creamy bokeh background, warm film grain, razor-sharp 8K. Japanese youth-style restrained, heart-fluttering, almost suffocating romantic atmosphere.0-4 seconds: Extremely slow push-in shot from medium desk view to side-profile close-up of the two students sitting side by side. Pure and innocent girl in summer school uniform, head slightly lowered as she focuses on writing notes. Long black hair with soft strands gently lifted by a breeze near her ear. Long eyelashes casting delicate shadows. Naturally flushed, soft skin. Corners of her mouth unconsciously curve upward in quiet concentration. Light, even breathing.4-9 seconds: Cut to the boy in close-up. School uniform collar slightly loosened, elbow on the desk, secretly turning his head to gaze at her. Eyes full of gentle, restrained affection and tenderness. Pupils slightly dilated. Adam’s apple bobs softly. Suddenly noticing her pen pause, he panics and quickly turns back to pretend to look at his own notes. Ear tips flush with a faint red. Fingertips tremble slightly as he grips the pen. Occasionally steals a glance at her from under his bangs. Breathing becomes slightly unsteady, lips pressed tightly as he tries to stay calm.9-15 seconds: Extreme dual close-up of both faces in the same frame, slow-motion. Their eyes suddenly meet. The girl slowly turns her head, first with a hazy, surprised expression, then quickly lowers her gaze in embarrassment for 0.3 seconds, gently biting her lower lip. Cheeks and earlobes instantly bloom with cherry-blossom pink. Moist eyelashes timidly lift as she looks back at him. At the same time, she shyly whispers in a soft voice, “......What are you looking at?” The boy freezes completely, pupils dilating, stunned for 0.4 seconds, then stammers in a flustered whisper, “N... nothing.” The girl bites her lip again, steals another glance at him, and whispers even softer, “......You’re lying.” The boy pauses, then lets out a gentle sigh and replies tenderly, “......Just looking at you.” His mouth slowly curves into a shy, gentle, lopsided smile. Fine smile lines appear at the corners of his eyes. Breathing noticeably deeper. An invisible electric current seems to crackle between their faces, pulling them together with thick, ambiguous tension. They share each other’s breath and warmth. The background completely melts into layered creamy dreamlike light spots and a warm glowing haze filled with floating fine particles.Lip sync is perfectly natural and precise. Emotional micro-expressions and breathing are synchronized. Dialogue delivered in low-energy, shy whispers with natural pauses of 200 - 400 milliseconds. Mouths move only when speaking no exaggeration, no robotic feel, perfectly natural lip-sync with authentic emotion.Overall audio: Distant summer cicada sounds faintly in the background, soft scratching of pen on paper, almost inaudible low-frequency heartbeats from both, and finally a gentle fade-in of airy piano. Dialogue is completely natural whispered lines embedded in the scene. Girl’s voice is soft, sweet, and shy. Boy’s voice shifts from panicked stuttering to gentle warmth.Throughout the entire clip, characters remain fully consistent in identity. Realistic subtle head tilts, eye movements, and synchronized breathing. No text, watermarks, or subtitles. Pure Japanese teenage secret crush, heart-fluttering suspense.

prompts.text: Seedance 2.0 prompt share: NASA APOLLO SPACESUIT A7L "WORN ON ANOTHER WORLD" DNA: July 20, 1969. 102 hours, 45 minutes, 40 seconds into the mission. One small step. Arri Alexa 65. Ultra-wide. Grain progressive — starts clinical-clean, ends at maximum as the lunar surface appears. Key light: cold fluorescent Mission Control white. Secondary: harsh unfiltered solar light — no atmosphere to diffuse it. Flares: none in the lab sequence. One single overwhelming flare as the visor catches unfiltered sunlight on the lunar surface. Background: white clean room → vacuum of space → lunar surface at Tranquility Base. 00:00–00:02 · THE LAYERS A single thread of nylon being measured under a magnifying glass by a white-gloved technician's hand. Then: cut to the 21 layers of the A7L suit being assembled simultaneously — each layer materializing and wrapping the suit form: the liquid cooling garment first, its tubes threading through the fabric like a vascular system. Then the pressure bladder. Then the restraint layer. Then the thermal micrometeorite garment. Each layer distinct, each critical. Camera cross-section view through all 21 layers simultaneously. 00:02–00:04.5 · THE HELMET Speed 30%. The polycarbonate helmet shell forms — perfectly spherical, flawless. The visor assembly drops in: the gold-coated visor — 24-karat gold, 0.0002 inches thick — pressing over the outer shell. Camera macro on the gold surface: it reflects everything in warm gold — including us. The neck ring locks with a quarter-turn — the mechanism designed to never, under any circumstances, fail. 00:04.5–00:07 · PRESSURIZATION Speed 8%. The most important moment. Air flowing into the suit — the pressure building to 3.75 psi. Camera inside the suit as it pressurizes: the fabric stiffening, the gloves expanding slightly. Every seal tested by the pressure itself. The suit becomes a world — a personal atmosphere, the only thing between a human being and the void. 00:07–00:10 · THE CLEAN ROOM Speed 15%. The suited figure — complete — standing in the white clean room under brutal fluorescent light. Technicians moving around it in blurred background. The suit reads in extraordinary detail: the layers visible at the seams, the connector ports, the PLSS backpack life support system mounting points. A visor drops over the helmet. The astronaut disappears inside. 00:10–00:13 · TRANQUILITY BASE Speed 3%. The surface of the Moon. The suit boot pressing into lunar regolith in ultra-slow motion — the print forming in dust that has not been disturbed in 4.5 billion years. Camera at surface level — the boot print in sharp focus, the horizon of the Moon in the background, the Earth hanging above it, the size of a marble. The suit in the background, the gold visor catching unfiltered solar light. The single most overwhelming flare of any film in this collection — total, white, sacred. 00:13–00:14.5 · THE REVEAL Speed 1% — absolute stillness. The A7L floating in the void — the Earth behind it at distance. The gold visor reflects the Earth. The Earth reflected in the suit designed to walk on the Moon. Everything is contained in this one reflection. 00:14.5–00:15 · END CARD Silence — total. Then a single radio crackle. NASA worm logo. "Worn once. Changed everything." No grain — this moment is too clear, too real. Hold. Fade.

Rain-soaked New York street at night. Neon signs, streetlights reflecting on wet asphalt. Steam rising from manholes. Lens flares, motion blur. Dolby Vision HDR. 0.0s–2.5s: Extreme low-angle tracking shot — a lone female fighter strides down a narrow NYC street, rain pouring heavily. Leather jacket soaked, hair slicked back and dripping. Heels echo faintly on wet pavement. Camera tracks backward with subtle shake. Yellow taxi lights streak across puddles. Figures step out from alleyways and fire escapes, slowly surrounding her. She tilts her head, cracks her knuckles — calm, fearless expression. 2.6s–5.0s: Whip-pan — first attacker lunges. TIME REMAP: slow-motion as she pivots smoothly, dodging and delivering a sharp elbow strike. Water sprays on impact. Her jacket snaps with the motion. Another attacker crashes into a stack of trash bags and metal bins. Sparks flicker from a flickering streetlight overhead. 5.1s–7.5s: Drone shot — overhead view as she moves fluidly through multiple opponents. SLOW MOTION: precise kicks and spins land cleanly, bodies sliding across rain-slick asphalt. Steam swirls under golden streetlights. One attacker swings a bat — she catches it mid-swing, twists, and disarms them effortlessly. 7.6s–10.0s: 360° orbital shot — she leaps into a spinning kick, taking down two attackers at once. Camera circles her as another rushes from behind. Without turning, she blocks and counters instantly. Breath visible in the cold night air. Each strike hits in sync with a rising cinematic score. 10.1s–13.0s: First-person POV — the final opponent charges. SMASH CUT: rapid, close-range exchange in slow motion. Her final punch lands clean. Silence falls. Rain continues to pour. Slow push-in — she stands alone in the empty street, adjusts her jacket sleeve, exhales steadily. Low-angle shot. Eyes locked forward. Unshaken.

prompts.text: INFINITE FALL — Beer Catch [image1] Guy: lean young man, wavy blonde hair, thin glasses, black short-sleeve open shirt, dark grey pinstripe wide-leg trousers, large silver belt buckle, brown leather loafers, arm tattoos, silver bracelets. Expression: not panicked — annoyed at the bottle, nothing more. IMAX 65mm aggressive handheld — camera itself in freefall with him, shaking slightly with air resistance, never still. Fast orbital cuts, whip pans between angles, camera sometimes rushing past him at speed. Everything blown violently upward: hair, jacket, trouser legs, shirt — continuous strong upward wind throughout. The visual grammar of terminal velocity. Sound FX: constant roaring wind, fabric snapping, bottle tumbling, liquid sloshing. Environment: pure white infinite void — no ground, no ceiling, no horizon. Just white in all directions. A brown glass beer bottle tumbling slowly in freefall beside him, liquid sloshing inside, just out of reach. negative: no ground, no slow camera, no calm floating — this is a violent fall The entire sequence is one continuous fall at full speed. Camera whips around him — bug's eye from directly below looking up at him shrinking then rushing toward camera, overhead looking straight down at him, 10mm close pass inches from his face with the wind tearing at his hair and glasses, Dutch angle tracking his full body as he reaches. The bottle tumbles just past his fingers — he repositions fast, body rotating in the fall, reaching again. His glasses nearly torn off by the wind, he pushes them back with one hand without stopping reaching with the other. The fall feels violent and fast — not peaceful zero gravity, not serene floating. The roaring wind is constant and loud. His clothes are being destroyed by the air resistance — shirt billowing completely open, trouser legs flattened against his legs then snapping outward. He finally grabs the bottle in one hard grip — fingers closing around the neck. He pulls it against the wind to his lips. Takes a long defiant sip. Wind still roaring. Hair still destroyed. Glasses still crooked. Camera does one final fast orbit around him — close, aggressive, whipping past. He lowers the bottle. Looks directly into the camera lens from centimeters away. Completely unbothered. Wind roar continues. Cut to black. prompts.text: FORMAT: 15s / 148 BPM / ONE CONTINUOUS SHOT / 3D action-comedy / Pixar-Kung Fu Hustle homage SUBJECTS: Young man, torn t-shirt. Girlfriend, floral dress. Boss, black suit. Blockers: Landlady in nightgown, Tailor, Mahjong duo, Coolie porter, Landlord in pajamas. Pixar-proportioned: rubbery limbs, wire-fu physics. PROPS: Rainbow lollipop, silver hatchet, red slipper, cigarette, brass forearm rings, mahjong tiles, wooden pole. ENVIRONMENT: 1930s walled tenement block: dusty courtyard, tight corridors, cascading balconies. Laundry lines, hanging signs. Dusty golden light. MOOD: Wire-fu comedic mayhem. Impossible physics, deadpan reactions. COLOR LOGIC: Golden Hour Look CAMERA: One uninterrupted Steadicam event. Tracks the young man continuously, pulling back as he runs, swinging to frame each blocker without cutting. 24mm spherical lens. SCENE: 1. Steadicam starts MCU. Young man hands girlfriend the lollipop. 2. Boss steps in raising the hatchet. Young man leaps ten feet backward. Camera pulls back fast into the alley to lead his sprint. 3. Landlady steps in, swinging a red slipper in a blurry tornado of strikes. Young man slides under the swings on both knees. The wind force of her slaps blasts the Boss backward. 4. Camera tracks backward into a corridor. Tailor blocks, brass rings clinking. Young man deflects rapid punches, spinning the Tailor into a pillar as camera glides past. 5. Mahjong duo attacks with synchronized rapid-fire palm strikes. Young man parries both simultaneously using the back of his hands, then does a wire-fu backflip twenty feet up. Camera tilts up as they crash into their tile table. 6. Camera levels on a balcony. Coolie thrusts a wooden pole like a spear. Slow motion: Young man deflects the tip with a single knuckle. Normal speed: he spins the pole away, plants it, and pole-vaults over the roof. 7. Camera tracks him landing on a vertical brick wall. Three thugs launch flying kicks. Young man runs horizontally along the wall, blocking their kicks with rapid shin-blocks in mid-air. 8. Camera drops to floor level. Boss charges, swinging a wild hatchet combo. Young man side-steps, traps the wrist, steps directly onto the falling blade, and leaps off the Boss's head. 9. Camera pulls back through the gate. Landlord attacks with heavy tai-chi pushes. Young man engages in a lightning-fast sticky-hands exchange, redirecting the Landlord's momentum to spin him away before running past. 10. Camera stops EWS on open street. Boss and thugs crash into the Landlady in a dust cloud. Girlfriend waves the lollipop from a window. He waves back, running away. SFX: Acoustic guitar opens. Slipper slaps beat 3, brass clink 4, rapid palm smacks and tile crash 5, slow-mo whoosh and wood clack 6, fast wall steps and kick thuds 7, metallic ping 8, heavy clothing swoosh 9, massive dust boom 10 with guitar reprise.

prompts.text: This is the prompt used in Seedance 2.0 FORMAT: 15s / MULTI-CUT / 5 BEATS / VIRAL EMOTIONAL TWIST SUBJECTS: A small robot the size of a shoebox, boxy body made of dented brushed aluminum with visible rivets and scratches, one flickering blue LED eye (left) and one steady warm orange LED eye (right), two stubby telescoping arms with three-pronged claw hands, and tank treads that squeak when moving. Its chest panel has a cracked circular speaker grille. It moves with jerky stop-start motions and tilts its whole body to express emotion. A single wilted daisy in a cracked terra cotta pot — this is the visual anchor throughout. Stylized 3D quality animation with tactile material rendering, squash-and-stretch on the robot's body, and exaggerated emotional eye animation. ENVIRONMENT: An abandoned rooftop greenhouse at golden hour. Shattered glass panels let warm sunset light pour in at low angles. Overgrown dead vines cover rusted metal shelving. Cracked concrete floor with patches of dry soil. One corner has a small puddle of collected rainwater reflecting the orange sky. Dust motes and tiny pollen particles float in the light beams. The city skyline is visible through broken glass — distant but soft, out of focus. STYLE: Stylized 3D animation, subsurface rendering on organic matter, physically accurate metal wear on the robot. Warm desaturated palette — dusty oranges, faded greens, soft rust tones. Cinematic depth of field with golden hour lens flares. Gentle film grain. MOOD: Lonely tenderness building to quiet joy. Bittersweet but ultimately hopeful. COLOR LOGIC: Sunset Rust — warm amber light, cool blue-grey shadows, pops of green only at the very end. ⸻ 0:00–0:02 · The Discovery Wide shot, 35mm, low angle from floor level. The greenhouse is still, bathed in golden light. The tiny robot rolls in through a gap in the broken glass wall, treads squeaking. It stops. Its mismatched eyes scan the space — the blue one flickers nervously. It spots something offscreen. Cut to insert close-up, 85mm: the wilted daisy in its cracked pot, sitting alone on a shelf in a beam of light. One brown petal falls. SFX: tread squeak, servo whir, gentle wind through broken glass, petal tap on concrete. 0:02–0:05 · The Attempt Medium shot, 50mm. The robot rolls to the shelf and extends one arm toward the pot. Too short. It stretches — whole body tilting forward on its treads, arm telescoping to maximum with a strained ratcheting sound. Fingertips barely touch the pot. It nudges the pot off the shelf and catches it with both claws in a clumsy fumble — nearly drops it, recovers, hugs it tight against its chest panel. Its orange eye glows slightly brighter. SFX: ratchet extension, ceramic scrape, fumble clatter, catch clank, relieved servo sigh. 0:05–0:08 · The Problem Close-up, 85mm, on the daisy. It is completely wilted — drooping, brown, dry. The robot tilts its body sideways examining it. It pokes one petal with a claw tip. The petal crumbles to dust. The robot recoils. Its blue eye flickers faster — distressed. It looks around the greenhouse frantically, body swiveling left and right. Then it spots the puddle of rainwater in the corner. Both eyes lock on it. SFX: petal crumble, distressed beep sequence, servo whip-pan, hopeful double chirp. 0:08–0:12 · The Gift Medium tracking shot, 35mm, following the robot as it rolls carefully toward the puddle, pot clutched tight. It arrives at the edge. Problem: it has no way to scoop water. One beat of stillness. Then it tilts the entire pot and dips the dry soil directly into the shallow puddle — gentle, slow, deliberate. Water seeps into the cracked terra cotta. The robot holds it there. Sunset light catches the water surface, throwing rippled golden reflections across the robot's dented body. Its speaker grille crackles and emits a faint broken hum — it is trying to sing. SFX: water absorption, gentle ripple, crackling hum melody attempt, distant wind. 0:12–0:15 · The Bloom Close-up, 85mm. The robot lifts the pot from the water and holds it at eye level. Nothing happens. One still beat. Then — a single green leaf unfurls from the stem, small and bright against all the brown. The robot's blue eye stops flickering and holds steady for the first time. Both eyes glow warm together. It pulls the pot closer to its chest. Camera slowly pulls back to a wide shot, 35mm. The tiny robot sits alone in the vast greenhouse, sunset light wrapping around it, holding one small pot with one new leaf. prompts.text: FORMAT: 15s / 150 BPM / 8 shots / compact action duel loop SUBJECTS: One occult fighter and one curse-like creature, both drawn as 2.5D line-art characters with visible contour lines, interior sketch lines and light hatching, never solid black fill, one body each in every beat. SCENE: Black and white 3D sketch-anime combat inside a minimal sketch ruin on white paper. Keep clear 2.5D line-art characters with contour lines, interior construction strokes and light hatching, not black silhouette bodies. Start on direct impact, not entry, with both characters already in mid-exchange at center frame. Use aggressive cinematic framing, hard impact punctuation, sharp micro-pauses, strong anticipation and forceful follow-through while preserving left-right continuity and readable strike lanes. The creature uses short curse bursts, limb warping and ink shockwaves. Build the action as a seamless loop so the final rush reconnects directly into the opening clash. The space has floor, broken wall planes and depth, and only redraws on hits, surges or skids. MOOD: Occult pressure, supernatural force, hard cinematic impact, seamless loop energy. COLOR LOGIC: Monochromatic Grading STYLE: 3D hand-drawn sketch anime with 2.5D line-art characters, bold cinematic action framing and readable curse-battle choreography TIMELINE: 1. Smash cut, low 24mm impact track, open on direct mid-clash at center frame as fighter's short strike and creature's forearm collide, lines splinter outward, both bodies compress then snap past each other without stopping, SFX: impact snap, brush tear. 2. Hard cut, 35mm handheld push, fighter pivots out of the pass, shoulder-feints and lands a short body strike under guard, both recoil half a step with visible force transfer, SFX: air slice, ink thud. 3. Whip pan, 50mm side track, creature whips a warped forearm across a clear lane and sheds a short ink shockwave, fighter slips under both by inches, SFX: heavy whoosh, brush tear, ink flare. 4. Smash cut, 28mm close pursuit, micro-pause, fighter plants, twists through the hips and drives a compact rib counter, impact distortion spikes and the camera kicks with contact, SFX: crack hit, ink burst. 5. Match cut, 40mm rear three-quarter, creature skids backward as floor and wall lines redraw under the impact path, SFX: scrape, paper rip, low ink pulse. 6. Hard cut, 32mm handheld orbit, creature slams back in with one arm warping longer, fighter gives ground, parries high and pivots across the axis to keep continuity, SFX: double hit, sharp breath, tendon stretch. 7. Whip pan, 65mm impact close-up, fighter coils low, holds one sharp micro-pause, then releases a decisive upward strike, recoil whips through both bodies and the frame blows out white for a beat, SFX: deep crack, white flash burst. 8. Hard cut, 24mm wide pursuit frame, creature regathers, fires a short chest-level curse burst and surges back to center as fighter rebounds into the same opposing rush geometry as beat 1, SFX: trailing crack, paper hiss, ink burst, rushing foot drag.

Only black speed lines, impact rings, smear frames, skid marks, and sharp red blood accents. Clean negative space keeps every move instantly readable. MOOD: Brutal, explosive, relentless, stylish, unfinished. COLOR LOGIC: Monochromatic Grading TIMELINE: 0:00-0:01 - Wide shot, extreme negative space. The lean fighter stands centered and still. The heavy fighter drops from above already throwing a downward strike. Sudden hard push-in. 24mm wide feel. SFX: air drop, hard land, cutting whoosh. 0:01-0:03 - CUT ON ACTION. Side wide shot. Heavy fighter unleashes jab, hook, knee. Lean fighter slips, guards, absorbs the knee, then fires back with calf kick, straight punch, spinning back kick. A sharp red blood arc snaps off the final hit. Short truck move. 35mm feel. SFX: swishes, dry thuds, foot taps, impact ticks. 0:03-0:05 - SMASH CUT. Medium wide side view. Heavy fighter answers with body hook, elbow, backfist, stomp kick, then drives through with a rushing shoulder check, forcing the lean fighter across frame. Quick red flecks burst near the impact rings. Fast lateral move with slight undercrank feel. SFX: impact cracks, whip swishes, stomp hit, air bursts. 0:05-0:07 - CUT ON ACTION. Side wide shot. Lean fighter ducks the next swing, steps inside, lands a rib shot, slicing elbow to the chin, then a rising kick to the chest. A brief red spray snaps off the last connection. Short truck move. 35mm film feel. SFX: duck swish, body thud, elbow crack, kick crack, skid scrape. 0:07-0:10 - WHIP PAN TRANSITION. Side wide shot. Both crash back together and trade a savage twelve-hit chain: punch, block, elbow, knee, duck, backfist, kick, catch, shove, hook, spinning elbow, straight cross. Red flicks burst only on the hardest impacts. Fast truck move with momentum-based cutting. Thick black impact circles on the heaviest blows. SFX: rapid hit flurry, hard swishes, bass ticks, breath bursts. 0:10-0:12 - CUT ON ACTION. Worm's-eye wide shot. Heavy fighter surges forward again. Lean fighter eats two hits, slips the third, steps off the planted thigh, vaults upward, and hammers down. Both collide midair in a tight X-shaped silhouette that splits apart instantly. Quick arc move around the clash. 24mm wide feel. SFX: rising whoosh, hit flurry, double crack, burst hiss, bass slam. 0:12-0:15 - HARD CUT. Monumental wide shot. Both land already in motion, skid a step, rebound, and charge back to center without pause, dissolving into black strike smears and red flecks as the exchange continues. Tiny push-in. End mid-fight, unresolved. 50mm standard feel. SFX: skid scrape, hard swishes, dry impacts, low ring.

prompts.text: Prompt Seedance 2.0: A cinematic shot of a young man and woman standing at the edge of a dark, vast body of water. The woman has long blonde hair and is wearing a long, two-toned tan and brown coat. The man has dark, wavy hair and wears a dark overcoat. Behind them in the distance is a large suspension bridge (resembling the Bosphorus Bridge in Istanbul) illuminated with bright red lights, alongside a faint city skyline with minarets. Initially, the couple is intensely arguing. Suddenly, a glowing object streaks from the sky and crashes into the water near the bridge, creating a massive, explosive plume of water. A colossal, towering tsunami wave forms and surges rapidly toward the couple. Realizing their impending doom, they stop arguing, turn to each other, and share a passionate, dramatic kiss as the giant wave rises directly behind them and ultimately crashes over the camera, plunging the screen into dark, turbulent water.Color and LightingCinematic, moody color grading. The color palette is heavily dominated by cool, desaturated teal and cyan tones in the sky and the water, creating an apocalyptic and melancholic atmosphere. This is sharply contrasted by the glowing warm red lights of the suspension bridge in the background and the natural warm skin tones of the couple, creating a classic teal-and-orange cinematic contrast. The lighting is overcast twilight, soft but dramatic.Sound and Audio EffectsThe audio begins with the muffled, frantic sounds of a couple shouting and arguing. At 0:02, there is a sharp, massive low-frequency boom and a whooshing sound as the meteor impacts the water, followed by the deep, rumbling sound of millions of gallons of water splashing and a wave building.MusicAs the massive wave begins to form (around 0:04), an emotional, soaring pop-rock ballad begins to play, dominating the audio mix. The song features strong vocals singing dramatic lyrics about the end of the world (“Just stop your crying, it’s a sign of the times / We gotta get away from here” - specifically, “Sign of the Times” by Harry Styles). The music swells to an emotional crescendo as the couple kisses and the wave crashes.

prompts.text: Create a cinematic one-take frozen-time house party video, maximum 15 seconds. Do not copy his identity or complexion onto the crowd. The crowd is mixed and varied with many different ethnicities, skin tones, hairstyles, outfits, and body types. One continuous unbroken reverse tracking shot: the camera moves backward in front of the main man as he moves toward it, but he does not walk nonstop. The scene is a dark stylish house party with warm practical lamps, deep shadows, club-like background light, and a consistent direct on-camera flash locked on the main man so he stays bright and crisp. 0–2s: The party is moving for a brief moment. The main man looks into camera, raises one hand, and aggressively snaps his fingers. On the exact snap, everyone around him instantly freezes mid-party: dancing, laughing, holding cups, leaning, posing, talking. 2–5s: He walks forward two steps, then turns left toward a frozen man beside him. He calmly fixes the man’s jacket collar with both hands, pats it flat, gives a small approving look, then turns back toward camera. 5–8s: He continues forward, pauses beside a frozen woman holding a red party cup. He gently takes the red cup from her hand, takes one quick casual sip, then tosses the empty cup neatly into a nearby trash bin while she remains frozen. 8–12s: He steps forward again, turns toward another frozen guest holding a cell phone. He takes the phone, angles it toward himself like he is checking the camera or recording the moment, smirks at it, then keeps it in hand as he turns back toward camera. 12–15s: He stops center frame, raises his snapping hand again, looks directly into camera, and snaps his fingers a second time. On the snap, the party instantly comes back to life around him while he remains calm and stylish. Keep the frozen guests perfectly still except objects he touches. Natural fabric motion, realistic hand contact, clean party atmosphere, no text, no logo focus, no identity blending, normal proportions.

Movement style: a fusion of assassin precision and supernatural speed — sharp, controlled, yet overwhelmingly fast.S ENVIRONMENT: A dark collapsing dungeon corridor transforming into a fractured warzone. Stone walls cracking, debris falling, sparks flying, embers drifting in air. Narrow pathways constantly breaking apart under pressure. CAMERA (CRITICAL): NO STATIC CAMERA — ALWAYS MOVING Primary: over-the-shoulder forward chase shot Camera trails slightly behind, constantly correcting position Frequent overshoot → snap back → side drift Dynamic tilt and roll, unstable framing Heavy forward motion drag, lens warp, rolling shutter distortion Camera feels like it is struggling to keep up with the warrior’s speed ACTION TIMELINE (15s CONTINUOUS FORWARD ASSAULT) 0.0–1.2s — IMPACT ENTRY Warrior bursts through a collapsing stone wall already sprinting at full speed. Instant chain-blade sweep clears enemies ahead mid-run. Camera slams forward behind with heavy shake and dust explosion. 1.2–2.8s — ROTATIONAL CUTTING DRIVE Warrior spins while still advancing forward. Chains extend outward forming a rotating vortex of slicing energy. Enemies are cut apart in a circular motion while forward momentum continues. Camera briefly arcs sideways, then snaps back behind. 2.8–4.5s — PHASE DASH STRIKE Warrior flickers forward in rapid bursts, leaving afterimages behind. Afterimages continue attacking enemies while main body advances ahead. Camera lags, then aggressively accelerates to catch up. 4.5–6.2s — WALL-RUN ADVANCE Warrior runs along the side wall without losing forward direction. Chains whip downward and forward, striking enemies below and ahead. Camera tilts sideways ~45° maintaining unstable forward tracking. 6.2–8.0s — GROUND SHRED CHARGE Warrior lands and drags blades along the ground while sprinting. Sparks explode continuously, debris kicks backward violently. Low-angle camera chase emphasizes speed and impact. 8.0–10.0s — SPEED FRACTURE BURST Warrior accelerates into near-invisible motion, becoming a streak of energy. Environment fractures open as enemies are sliced instantly. Camera struggles heavily, frame distortion and motion tearing visible. 10.0–12.0s — AERIAL FORWARD STRIKE Warrior leaps forward (no vertical pause), mid-air chain slam clears path ahead. Shockwave pushes debris outward while forward momentum continues. Camera rises slightly then dives forward aggressively. 12.0–13.5s — MULTI-LANE ATTACK Afterimages split into left and right lanes attacking simultaneously. Main warrior continues straight forward at full speed. Camera zig-zags trying to follow multiple targets. 13.5–15.0s — UNSTOPPABLE EXIT Warrior accelerates beyond frame and partially disappears ahead. Camera whips forward trying to catch up but fails. FINAL FRAME: pure forward motion blur stretching environment → hard cut to black mid-run

prompts.text: Want to know how to achieve this insane level of cinematic detail and fluid dynamics using Seedance 2.0? Here is the exact prompt I used! Subject: > A large, shaggy-haired dog and a real white duck, both completely free of leashes or harnesses. Both animals are soaking wet, with water visibly dripping from the dog's heavy coat and beading off the duck's waxy feathers. Action: > The dog and duck enter the house together. In the center of the room, they both stop for a synchronized grooming moment. In extreme slow motion, the dog starts a powerful head-to-tail shake, creating a massive, spiraling spray of water droplets. Simultaneously, the duck stands tall, stretches its neck, and vigorously flaps its wings to shake off the rain, sending smaller, fine droplets into the air. The two overlapping sprays of water create a beautiful, chaotic pattern of liquid physics as they catch the light. Camera & Movement: > Fixed low-angle cinematic shot. The camera is placed at floor level to emphasize the scale of the animals and the trajectory of the water droplets. High-speed camera aesthetic (slow motion) to capture every ripple in the dog's skin and every individual feather movement of the duck. prompts.text: EL TAQUERORON SEEDANCE 2.0 — TEXT TO VIDEO — 15 SECONDS — 21:9 ASPECT SHOT 00:00–00:02 · LA TAQUERÍA Extreme close-up macro — the trompo al pastor turning in the early morning light. The meat glistening, the charcoal glow behind it, the pineapple on top catching the fire light. Camera pulls back slowly: Chuy's taquería in Tepito, 6am. Chuy behind the counter — white apron, red bandana on forehead, arms crossed. The trompo turning. The comal hot. The cilantro and onion chopped and waiting. A line of workers, construction helmets and lunchboxes, waiting for their tacos. The trompo spins. Faster than it should. SHOT 00:02–00:04.5 · LA SEÑAL The last customer in line receives his taco. Chuy looks at the trompo — now empty of customers but still turning. He touches the trompo's base with one hand. It vibrates. The pineapple on top begins glowing — not orange from the fire, but supernatural gold. The charcoal fire intensifies: the coals glowing white-hot. The cilantro and onion on the cutting board lift off and orbit the trompo slowly. The salsa jars rattle. The hot sauce begins glowing red. SHOT 00:04.5–00:08 · LA TRANSFORMACIÓN Speed 40%. The trompo IS the transformation's axis — everything builds around its rotation. The vertical spit becomes the robot's spine. The stacked meat panels unfold outward from the spit like a flower — each layer of al pastor becoming one armor plate, the seasoning visible in the texture of each panel, the achiote red and the pineapple gold. The charcoal grill base spreads outward, becoming the robot's legs — the grill grates forming foot soles that leave scorch marks on the street. The comal rises and becomes a shield in the robot's right arm. The enormous carving knife that Chuy uses to slice the taco meat — it rises and becomes the robot's sword, still glowing from the fire. The pineapple on top of the trompo becomes the robot's head — glowing gold, with charcoal-fire eyes. Chuy in the head pod: visible inside the pineapple, red bandana still on, white apron. The hot sauce bottles orbit the robot's shoulders. Sparks fly in achiote red and charcoal orange. prompts.text: Seedance V2 It is really fun to do long videos but you need to do some editing to get the best out of the clips, I did not do any editing with this video. This is the firs Clip prompt Shoot this like a prestige streaming thriller, not a music video, not fantasy. Two women, both idols, both adults. The scene lives in breath, silence, and proximity. Set the entire moment in a dim vintage apartment hallway, or the corner of an old room that feels half-forgotten. Deep walnut wood paneling. Antique brass wall sconces. One warm amber pool of light falls over the women while everything beyond it dies into shadow. The space should feel beautiful, expensive, and airless, as if the room itself is closing around them. Character one is Han Seo-rin, early 30s, a Korean female idol with an elegant but quietly dangerous presence. She wears a black turtleneck under a long black coat, all clean lines and dark restraint. Her hair is sleek, dark, and softly layered around the face, with a slight fringe that lets her eyes appear and disappear in the low light. She is not loud. She is the kind of woman who controls a room by lowering her voice. Character two is Tachibana Rei, 25, a Japanese female idol with a pale, fragile beauty that reads delicate at first glance but emotionally intelligent on closer look. She wears an ivory V-neck knit dress that falls to the knees, soft and understated, the fabric catching the warm light. Her long dark hair is slightly disordered, as though the evening has already worn her down. She looks like someone trying very hard not to show fear. The emotional shape is simple: suspicion, pressure, fixation. No overt violence. No grabbing. No melodrama. The tension comes from how little space Seo-rin leaves Rei to breathe. Open on Rei already standing near the wall beneath the sconce, shoulders tight, breathing shallow, gaze lowered but restless. Then let Seo-rin enter behind her, close enough to dominate the frame without touching. She stops just at Rei’s back, almost still, letting the silence do the work. The camera should feel like it is slowly being pulled toward them. Seo-rin leans in toward Rei’s ear, speaking so softly that it feels more dangerous than a shout. One hand rises near Rei’s cheek, almost brushing it, but never quite landing. Keep that hesitation. That is where the charge is. Rei’s hands tense near her chest. Her fingers curl. Her jaw tightens. She looks away, then toward the doorway, then down again, realizing there is nowhere easy to go. Use close shots of the details that matter: the tremor in Rei’s fingers, the flicker in her eyes, the shadow of Seo-rin’s face falling across her neck, the black silhouette of the coat swallowing the warm light, the tiny pause before a breath, the way Rei tries to stay composed and fails by a fraction. Dialogue should feel intimate, dangerous, and controlled. Seo-rin, near Rei’s ear, almost gentle: “You can run from everyone else. Not from me.” Seo-rin, after the smallest pause: “Stay where I can see you.” Rei, voice unsteady, trying to hold herself together: “Please... just let me leave.” Seo-rin, with the faintest smile, certain of the answer before she speaks: “You already know this is where the story ends.” Performance note: Seo-rin is never frantic, never theatrical, never raising her voice. Her control is what makes her frightening. Rei is not weak, just cornered; she should feel intelligent, proud, and increasingly shaken, fighting to keep her dignity in a moment that is slipping out of her hands. Visual tone: premium psychological thriller, shallow depth of field, slow deliberate camera drift, warm practical light against surrounding darkness, realistic skin texture, subtle fabric movement, no camp, no exaggerated acting. The scene should feel like a forbidden, dangerous beat from an expensive late-night TV drama.

prompts.text: Childhood nightmare unlocked...cat master fixed it (made with Seedance 2 on @nemovideoai ) Prompt share / #NemoOneShotChallenge / Seedance 2 Prompt (15 seconds total, each shot ~0.6–1.2s) Cinematic dark fairy-tale thriller with comedic twist, eerie enchanted forest, low-key lighting, cold moonlight filtering through dense trees, volumetric fog, high contrast shadows, dynamic handheld camera, expressive character animation, fast-paced storytelling. S1 (0.9s) Wide shot: An orange cat older brother in blue overalls and a gray flat cap runs barefoot through a dark forest, pulling along a white cat little sister in a dirty pink dress, both breathing heavily. S2 (0.8s) Rear tracking shot: The forest behind them echoes with distant howling wolves, shadows shifting between trees. S3 (0.9s) Forward reveal: Through the fog, a glowing candy house made of sweets appears at the end of the path, colorful and surreal against the dark woods. S4 (0.7s) Close-up: The siblings slow down, eyes wide—fear mixed with curiosity. S5 (0.8s) Door action: The orange cat cautiously pushes open the candy door, it creaks softly. S6 (0.9s) Interior wide: Inside, dim warm light reveals a strange room—giant half-open birdcage, scattered sweets, and a bed in the corner. S7 (0.8s) Close-up: On the bed lies a white-haired “grandma” in green pajamas and a white shower cap, blanket half covering her face. S8 (0.9s) Dialogue moment: The “grandma” weakly gestures toward the birdcage, implying there is cake nearby, voice soft and inviting. S9 (0.8s) Insert shot: A cake sits temptingly near the open birdcage door. S10 (1.0s) Action split: The little sister eagerly reaches for the cake, while the orange cat narrows his eyes, scanning the room. S11 (0.9s) Suspicion reveal: Close-up at the foot of the bed—a wolf tail sticks out from beneath the blanket. S12 (1.0s) Action burst: The orange cat instantly grabs a nearby large iron shovel, swings it with full force toward the “grandma’s” head. S13 (1.0s) Impact & reveal: The shower cap flies off—“grandma” leaps up in pain, revealing a ferocious wolf face, snarling before panicking. S14 (1.0s) Escape: The wolf stumbles and scrambles out the door, fleeing into the dark forest. S15 (1.2s) Final comedic beat: The orange cat scratches the back of his head proudly, while the little sister happily eats cake beside him, cheering with crumbs on her face. Cat master vs father-in-law—straight chaos 
(made with 
@yapper_so
 Seedance 2)
Prompt share 

1990s Japanese TV drama style. A white cat (daughter, wearing a pink dress) sits beside her boyfriend, an orange cat (wearing a gray suit). Next to the father, a black bear (wearing casual clothes), sits the mother, a white rabbit (wearing a kimono). All four characters speak entirely in English. A 15-second multi-cut scene that builds awkward tension and erupts into absurd comedy.
A typical cramped Japanese dining room, with a table packed full of homemade dishes.
The four characters are tightly squeezed around the small table. The orange cat boyfriend sits stiffly, forcing a nervous smile. The black bear father crosses his arms, glaring intensely at him with growing suspicion.
Breaking the heavy silence, the daughter (white cat) beams with excitement and points proudly at her boyfriend:
“Dad! I want you to meet my boyfriend!”
The mother (white rabbit) smiles gently and pats the father’s shoulder, trying to calm him down:
“Dear… please don’t look so scary.”
The father slowly lowers his head. A long, ominous silence. Then suddenly—
He SLAMS the table, stands up violently, and roars:
“BOYFRIEND?!”
In an instant, chaos explodes. The black bear lunges across the table and starts wildly swinging at the orange cat. Plates fly into the air, food scatters everywhere in exaggerated slow motion. The orange cat desperately dodges and shields himself, shouting:
“WAIT—SIR—PLEASE—!”
In the corner, the white cat daughter and the white rabbit mother cling to each other, trembling and crying in panic:
“Dad, stop!!”
“This is too much!!”
The scene ends in full slapstick mayhem: overturned table, food everywhere, the bear still chasing the orange cat around the tiny room as everything collapses into absurd, explosive comedy.

prompts.text: Shot 1 (00: 00–00:01) – MS, Dolly in + Whip Pan A white-haired sorceress stands in an ancient archive filled with hanging talismans and bells, painting a sigil. Dark mist erupts from the ground—she reacts instantly, dodging and countering with a sweeping brush strike. VFX: Distorted, pulsing shadow mist. SFX: Paper rustle, soft bells, low hum. Shot 2 (00: 01–00:02) – CU, Fast Push-in Her eyes glow. With a flick of her wrist, she draws sharp blue sigil strokes mid-air, forming blade-like trails. VFX: Intersecting cold-blue energy lines. SFX: Sharp air cuts, energy charge. Shot 3 (00: 02–00:03) – WS, Crane Up Talismans swirl violently. Layered circular sigils form beneath her feet. A shadow entity emerges but is blocked by the rotating barrier. VFX: Multi-layer rotating sigil rings, vortex of talismans. SFX: Deep resonance, swirling wind. Shot 4 (00: 03–00:04) – MFS, Orbit Tracking Scene shifts to a fractured sky. She steps on floating sigils; her brush extends into a glowing chain of runes that lashes toward the entity. VFX: Flickering rune-chain light. SFX: Air tearing, chain clinks. Shot 5 (00: 04–00:06) – LS, Chase Cam Amid storm clouds and a broken moon, she rides the rune chain through the air, pursuing the fleeing shadow. VFX: Rolling clouds, blue-white trails vs black mist. SFX: Roaring wind, distant thunder. Shot 6 (00: 06–00:07) – CU, Slide She taps nodes along the chain, activating hidden purple sigils that pulse with new energy. VFX: Sequential purple node illumination, pulse flow. SFX: Light clicks, energy hum. Shot 7 (00: 07–00:08) – MCU, Static She closes in and strikes the entity’s forehead. A burst of light—its body distorts, a complex seal appears on its chest. VFX: Purple-blue flash, rotating seal. SFX: Sharp burst, distorted screech. Shot 8 (00: 08–00:09) – WS, Dive Shot Both streak downward like meteors, piercing clouds toward an ancient stone altar. VFX: Comet-like light trails. SFX: Air screech, compression. Shot 9 (00: 09–00:10) – WS, Impact Static They crash. Dust erupts. She slams her hand down—radiating sigils crack across the ground. VFX: Glowing fractures spreading outward. SFX: Heavy impact, stone cracking. Shot 10 (00: 10–00:12) – LS, Pull Back A massive 3D sigil array rises, forming layered barriers that trap the entity at the center. She stands calmly outside. VFX: Expanding geometric barriers, drifting particles. SFX: Low steady resonance. Shot 11 (00: 12–00:13) – CU, Static She forms a hand seal and whispers: “Seal.” VFX: Light particles contract. SFX: Soft chant, energy tightening. Shot 12 (00: 13–00:15) – CU, Fade Out Eyes closed, she meditates as all light fades, leaving faint residual glow in silence. VFX: Light dissipates into darkness. SFX: Gentle wind, fading echo.

One figure: a woman on a sand-skiff — a flat wooden board with a triangular sail, gliding across compacted sand on bone runners. She wears wrapped linen armor, copper goggles, a weighted net coiled at her waist. She watches the sand. [2–4s] ECU the sand surface — it's BREATHING. Rippling outward from a point 200 yards ahead. The sand rises like a slow dome. The sail-woman cuts the skiff hard right. The dome ERUPTS — a sandworm. 40 feet, segmented, chitinous plates the color of rust. [4–7s] Chase through the canyon — the skiff banks between sandstone pillars. The worm follows UNDERGROUND — you see its path as a moving ridge of sand, smashing through the earth, pillars cracking as it passes beneath their foundations. She throws the weighted net — it wraps around a sandstone tower, rope trailing to her skiff. [7–10s] The worm surfaces directly in the skiff's path. She leans the board, catches wind, and the skiff JUMPS — airborne over the worm's back. In mid-air she drives a barbed stake into the top of its head plate. Lands the skiff on the other side. Rope connects stake to the sandstone tower. [10–13s] The worm charges away — the rope goes taut against the tower. The tower HOLDS. The worm's momentum whiplashes it sideways. She brings the skiff alongside, pulls her goggles up. Beneath the goggles — calm, focused eyes. She draws a curved knife and begins cutting a single iridescent scale from the worm's flank — the harvest. That's all she came for. One scale. The worm hisses but doesn't fight. She pats its flank once, takes the scale, pushes off. The skiff catches wind. She vanishes between the sandstone towers. Cut to black. Ultra-realistic.

prompts.text: "A cinematic wild-animal action sequence in one continuous epic shot. Start with an ultra-wide aerial view above a stormy jungle canyon at dawn, mist pouring through the trees, waterfalls crashing into a river below, golden light cutting through dark clouds. On opposite cliffs, a massive tiger and a giant black gorilla lock eyes across the gap, both tense, powerful, and silent. The camera dives fast between them as thunder rolls. The tiger leaps first, using a fallen tree as a bridge, while the gorilla smashes through vines and rock to meet it. They collide on a narrow cliff ledge in a burst of dust, leaves, and flying stone. The camera circles tightly as they fight with speed and force, slipping near the edge while rain begins falling harder. Just as the ledge collapses beneath them, both launch apart onto separate rocks above the raging river. Final beat: they stop, turn, and look upward as an even larger shadow moves through the mist behind them." Instead of breaking it into scenes, everything is chained together: Aerial wide → fast dive → collision → fight → environmental collapse → final reveal What really matters here is motion continuity. Every action triggers the next: Camera dive leads into the clash Impact leads into close combat Environment starts breaking → forces separation Final pause sets up the last reveal That cause-and-effect flow is what keeps it from feeling random. What Makes This Work Single continuous camera movement (no hard cuts) Clear spatial geography (you always know where everything is) Momentum-driven choreography instead of static fighting Environment reacting to the action (dust, rain, collapsing ledge) Seedance 2.0 handles chaos much better when: Motion has a clear direction The camera has a defined path Big moments are spaced out (not everything happening at once) Too many disconnected actions = breaks immersion One flowing sequence = feels cinematic Why One-Shot Works So Well It forces the AI to: Maintain consistency Respect physics and spacing Keep the scene coherent over time Which is exactly where most generations usually fail. How to Create an Epic One-Shot Animal Battle in Seedance 2.0? Prompt Below! (Tiger vs Gorilla)

Tried building a full one-shot cinematic action sequence in Seedance 2.0 and no cuts, just continuous motion from start to finish.

The goal was to make it feel like a real long-take shot you’d see in a high-budget film.

Prompt:
"A cinematic wild-animal action sequence in one continuous epic shot. Start with an ultra-wide aerial view above a stormy jungle canyon at dawn, mist pouring through the trees, waterfalls crashing into a river below, golden light cutting through dark clouds. On opposite cliffs, a massive tiger and a giant black gorilla lock eyes across the gap, both tense, powerful, and silent. The camera dives fast between them as thunder rolls. The tiger leaps first, using a fallen tree as a bridge, while the gorilla smashes through vines and rock to meet it. They collide on a narrow cliff ledge in a burst of dust, leaves, and flying stone. The camera circles tightly as they fight with speed and force, slipping near the edge while rain begins falling harder. Just as the ledge collapses beneath them, both launch apart onto separate rocks above the raging river. Final beat: they stop, turn, and look upward as an even larger shadow moves through the mist behind them."

Instead of breaking it into scenes, everything is chained together:

Aerial wide → fast dive → collision → fight → environmental collapse → final reveal

What really matters here is motion continuity.

Every action triggers the next:

Camera dive leads into the clash

Impact leads into close combat

Environment starts breaking → forces separation

Final pause sets up the last reveal

That cause-and-effect flow is what keeps it from feeling random.

What Makes This Work

Single continuous camera movement (no hard cuts)

Clear spatial geography (you always know where everything is)

Momentum-driven choreography instead of static fighting

Environment reacting to the action (dust, rain, collapsing ledge)

Seedance 2.0 handles chaos much better when:

Motion has a clear direction

The camera has a defined path

Big moments are spaced out (not everything happening at once)

Too many disconnected actions = breaks immersion
One flowing sequence = feels cinematic

Why One-Shot Works So Well
It forces the AI to:

Maintain consistency

Respect physics and spacing

Keep the scene coherent over time

Which is exactly where most generations usually fail.

Feels like this approach is perfect for:

Action scenes

Creature fights

Trailer-style sequences

Curious if anyone else is experimenting with one-shot prompts instead of multi-cut edits.

Only two characters: my unseen first-person POV and @ Image1 sitting across from me. Natural ambient sound only: light restaurant noise, tableware, distant water, faint voices, chewing, spitting, rinsing, my laughter. Setting: Outdoor dining table beside West Lake, Hangzhou, near the water, calm daylight or soft late afternoon light. Real smartphone-video realism, grounded textures, realistic food, realistic body and hand motion, accurate chopstick use, accurate mouth movement, accurate eye focus. The lake stays visible to one side of frame. Character: @ Image1 is the only visible person. She can switch seamlessly between slightly fierce-cute and soft adorable. Lip sync, voice, expressions, and body language stay fully synchronized. Emotional arc: cheerful and relaxed while eating, then shocked disgust, then angry embarrassment. Table: Exactly 7 dishes on the table. One dish is the West Lake vinegar fish shown in @ Image2. @ Image1 is happily eating rice and the other dishes, but not the fish at first. The table feels full but readable. The fish dish remains clearly visible before I offer it to her. Camera: Entire video is from my seated first-person view across the table. My hand and chopsticks may enter frame naturally. Slight handheld micro-shake from breathing and laughter only, never chaotic. No third-person shots, no reverse shots, no overhead shots, no cutaways. Continuous believable framing centered on @ Image1 with part of the lake visible. Action: @ Image1 sits opposite me, happily eating from her bowl, enjoying rice and other dishes except the West Lake vinegar fish. She looks bright, playful, relaxed, cute. From first-person POV, I pick up one bite of the fish with chopsticks and slowly extend it toward her. She notices it immediately, trusts me, leans forward, opens her mouth happily, and makes a cute “aam” sound as she bites the fish. I gently pull the chopsticks and my hand back out of frame. She chews happily for about one second, expecting it to taste good. Then the taste hits. Her expression changes instantly into exaggerated but believable disgust. Her face shifts into a comedic purple-disgust reaction while staying within realistic live-action style. She quickly turns toward the lake and spits it out with repeated “ptui, ptui, ptui” sounds. The motion is fast, fluid, and continuous from chewing to rejection. The moment she starts spitting, I begin laughing in first-person POV and keep laughing through the whole reaction. My laughter sounds genuine, amused, and uncontrollable, coming from behind the camera. The camera shakes slightly from laughing. After spitting, @ Image1 sticks out her tongue in disgust, immediately grabs the water on the table, and rinses her mouth quickly. She looks offended, embarrassed, irritated, but still vivid and cute. After rinsing, she snaps into angry frustration, grabs the entire fish dish from the table, and throws it into the nearby lake in one continuous motion. Ending: She finishes the throw angrily, still facing the lake, clearly annoyed and feeling betrayed, while I remain in first-person POV laughing. Keep the action continuous and clean. No extra characters enter frame.
